- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is above recent high, reduce by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a low sentiment period, cap the overshoot at +3% above the immediate prior peak.  
- If forecast consistently underestimates true values in the last 5–7 days (especially after sentiment dips), apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 true values show strong upward trend, model should not lag beyond 2–3 days; adjust to align with recent momentum.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values followed by sharp rises, model should anticipate a 1–2 day lag in the true breakout.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8), avoid overfitting to short-term noise; use 3–5 day smoothing in forecast adjustments.
